title: Two-stage retrieval for quality complaint search
document: A quality analytics team indexes historical complaint narratives with a sentence-transformer bi-encoder. The top candidates are reranked with a cross-encoder so investigators can find similar cases, root causes, and corrective actions faster.

title: FAISS indexing for large complaint archives
document: This guide explains normalized dense embeddings, FAISS inner-product indexing, index persistence, and document metadata alignment for a large archive of manufacturing complaints.

title: NumPy cosine search for small demonstrations
document: For a small public portfolio demo, normalized embeddings and a NumPy matrix multiplication provide reliable cosine similarity without adding FAISS deployment complexity.

title: Cross-encoder reranking of root-cause records
document: A cross-encoder jointly reads a search query and each retrieved root-cause record. It produces a relevance score that can improve ordering among semantically similar candidates.

title: Bi-encoder semantic retrieval fundamentals
document: Bi-encoders encode queries and documents separately. Document vectors can be precomputed, making candidate retrieval fast enough for interactive semantic search and RAG pipelines.

title: Latency benchmarking for retrieval systems
document: Measure document embedding time, index build time, query encoding time, candidate retrieval time, cross-encoder reranking time, and total search latency across multiple top-k settings.

title: Recall at K for candidate retrieval
document: Recall at K measures how many known relevant documents appear within the first K retrieved candidates. High candidate recall is important because the reranker cannot recover a relevant document that was never retrieved.

title: MRR and nDCG for ranked search
document: Mean Reciprocal Rank rewards systems that place the first relevant result early. nDCG uses graded relevance and discounts useful documents that appear lower in the ranked list.

title: Manual error analysis for semantic search
document: Review ambiguous queries, keyword-only matches, semantically similar but wrong results, domain mismatch, missing context, and cross-encoder overconfidence. Record both successful and failed examples.

title: Responsible use of job matching models
document: Automated job and resume matching can reflect bias and incomplete information. Model scores must not be the sole basis for hiring, rejection, compensation, immigration, or employment decisions.

title: Machine learning engineer — information retrieval
document: Role requires Python, PyTorch, sentence-transformers, semantic search, vector databases, evaluation with MRR and nDCG, API development, and production monitoring.

title: Data scientist — quality analytics
document: Role focuses on complaint analytics, root-cause discovery, statistical analysis, dashboards, Python, SQL, machine learning, stakeholder communication, and corrective-action insights.

title: Applied AI engineer — RAG and reranking
document: Build retrieval-augmented generation applications using embedding models, hybrid search, cross-encoder reranking, prompt evaluation, grounded answers, citations, and observability.

title: NLP engineer — multilingual search
document: Develop multilingual semantic search, query understanding, transformer fine-tuning, hard-negative mining, ranking evaluation, and low-latency model serving.

title: Analytics engineer — manufacturing data
document: Create tested data models for manufacturing operations using SQL, dbt, Python, data quality checks, lineage, documentation, and business-facing metrics.

title: Quality engineer — corrective action systems
document: Investigate nonconformances, perform root-cause analysis, manage CAPA records, analyze supplier issues, verify corrective actions, and improve quality-system documentation.

title: Hybrid search with dense and keyword retrieval
document: Hybrid search combines semantic embeddings with lexical methods such as BM25. Score fusion can improve coverage for part numbers, error codes, acronyms, and natural-language descriptions.

title: Hard-negative mining for ranking models
document: Hard negatives are plausible but nonrelevant documents retrieved by a strong first-stage model. They are useful for training ranking models to distinguish subtle relevance differences.

title: MS MARCO MiniLM cross-encoder
document: The MS MARCO MiniLM reranker scores query-passage pairs jointly. It is commonly used as a compact second-stage reranker because it offers a practical quality and latency tradeoff.

title: MiniLM sentence embeddings
document: The all-MiniLM-L6-v2 sentence-transformer maps sentences and short documents into a compact embedding space and is practical for CPU-based portfolio demonstrations.

title: Search result monitoring and drift
document: Monitor query mix, empty-result rate, click or relevance feedback, latency percentiles, index freshness, score distributions, and ranking quality to detect search-system drift.

title: Knowledge-base search for corrective actions
document: A searchable corrective-action knowledge base helps quality teams retrieve similar failures, containment plans, verified root causes, supplier actions, and effectiveness checks.

title: RAG retrieval and citation grounding
document: A RAG system retrieves relevant passages before generation. Candidate recall, reranking quality, source attribution, and citation correctness strongly affect answer groundedness.

title: Deployment checklist for Hugging Face Spaces
document: Keep app.py and requirements.txt at the Space root, load pretrained models lazily, avoid training at startup, use a small public-safe dataset, cache the index, and document resource limitations.
